From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Hale <sarah@tritondata.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah / Carlos —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise, worked example plus key rules we follow for hosted API billing. This is the standard behavior for the public hosted tier; if you move to a dedicated contract some rounding/aggregation details can be adjusted in the agreement.

Key rules (short):
- "Input tokens" include system messages, user messages, and any tool call arguments that are passed into the model as part of the request (e.g., tools invoked synchronously where the tool payload is fed back into the model).
- "Output tokens" are tokens that the model generates as the response body. If a tool executes and returns content that is sent back from the model as generated text, that content is counted as output tokens for that request.
- If the tool result is written to an external resource and not re-injected into the model prompt, the tokens used by the tool execution are not billed as model output. (In practice: function-call metadata that stays outside the model path is not billed as output.)
- Rounding: billing is per-token granularity (we tokenize with our BPE tokenizer). We do not round up to fixed blocks; every partial token is accounted for as a full token once tokenized. Streaming: tokens are counted as they are generated by the model in the response stream — there is no additional aggregation rounding beyond the tokenizer's discrete tokens.

Worked example (your asked scenario):
1) System prompt: 80 tokens (setup / persona / behavior constraints) -> billed as input (80).
2) User prompt: 45 tokens -> billed as input (45).
3) Model initiates a tool call; tool payload (arguments passed into the tool) is 30 tokens — those arguments were part of the request, so billed as input (30).
4) Tool executes and returns a 120-token JSON result. If that tool result is injected back into the model as generated text (i.e., the model returns it as part of its response), those 120 tokens are billed as output for that response. If instead the tool wrote the 120-token result only to an external store and the model did not re-ingest it, those tokens are not billed as output.
5) Model final generation (excluding the tool payload) is 450 tokens total. If that 450-token response includes the 120-token tool content inline, then output = 450 (which includes the 120). If the tool portion is not re-sent as model output, the billed output would be 330 tokens.

So in the conservative path where tool output is returned inline, total billed tokens for that single request would be: input = 80 + 45 + 30 = 155, output = 450.

Notes on caching and repeated prompts: if you use prefix/KV caching (session-level caches) and the system prompt is satisfied from cache on subsequent requests, we do not re-bill the full system token cost for every request in that session — only the first request that populates the cache is billed for the full system prompt. However, billing is tied to model processing: if a cached KV is used and the backend avoids re-processing those tokens, the billed amount for subsequent requests will be lower. This is why heavy use of KV/prefix caching can materially reduce per-request billable input tokens for steady-state workloads.

Hope that helps. Marissa / Dev — do you want me to add an ASCII table to the rate card PDF with a few worked examples?
